chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from al-Ḥārith ibn al-Mughīrah, who said:

I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying: “Indeed, the knowledge that descended with Ādam (عليه السلام) was not raised away. No knowledgeable one dies except that he has bequeathed his knowledge. Indeed, the earth does not remain without a knowledgeable one.”

key_terms.آدَمَ: Ādam (عليه السلام), the first recipient mentioned in the chain of transmitted knowledge
key_terms.الْأَرْضَ: the earth, which is said never to remain without such a knower
key_terms.الْعِلْمَ: the divinely bestowed knowledge being discussed in the narration
key_terms.عَالِمٌ: a knowledgeable one who possesses and transmits this divine knowledge
key_terms.لَمْ يُرْفَعْ: was not taken away or removed from the earth
key_terms.نَزَلَ: descended from Allah, indicating revealed or heaven-sent knowledge
key_terms.وَرَّثَ: bequeathed or passed on as an inheritance

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show that the earth is never without a divinely guided knower?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the divinely bestowed knowledge given from the time of Ādam (عليه السلام) continues uninterrupted and is never removed from the earth. It teaches that whenever one divinely guided knower passes away, that knowledge is inherited by another, affirming the continuous presence of a divinely authorized scholar among creation.
